claim: Amazon RDS bills DB instance hours based on the type of DB instance you use (for example db.t3.micro or db.m4.large).
question: What decides the DB instance-hour part of an Amazon RDS bill?

evidence.quote: DB instance hours – Based on the type (e.g. db.t3.micro, db.m4.large) of the DB instance consumed.

claim: Amazon RDS bills storage per GB per month for the storage capacity you provision to the DB instance, prorated if you scale it within the month.
question: How is Amazon RDS storage billed?

evidence.quote: Storage (per GB per month) – Storage capacity you have provisioned to your DB instance.
If you scale your provisioned storage capacity within the month, your bill will be pro-rated.

claim: Storage I/O requests per month are a billing dimension only for Amazon RDS magnetic storage and Amazon Aurora.
question: When does Amazon RDS charge for I/O requests?

values.display: magnetic storage and Amazon Aurora only

evidence.quote: I/O requests per month – Total number of storage I/O requests (for Amazon RDS magnetic storage and Amazon Aurora only).

claim: Backup storage is the storage for automated backups and customer-initiated DB snapshots; a longer backup retention period or more snapshots increases it.
question: What increases Amazon RDS backup storage cost?

evidence.quote: Backup Storage – The storage associated with your automated database backups and any customer-initiated database snapshots.
Increasing your backup retention period or taking additional database snapshots increases the backup storage consumed by your database.

claim: Amazon RDS bills internet data transfer in and out of the DB instance.
question: Which data transfer does the Amazon RDS bill include?

values.display: Internet data transfer in and out

evidence.quote: Data transfer – Internet data transfer in and out of your DB instance.

claim: Data transfer between an Amazon EC2 instance and an RDS DB instance in different Availability Zones of the same Region is charged (standard EC2 Regional data transfer for the EC2 instance); there is no additional charge on the RDS side.
question: Is data transfer between EC2 and RDS in different Availability Zones charged?

evidence.quote: When data transfers between an Amazon EC2 instance and an Amazon RDS database instance in different Availability Zones of the same Region, data transfer charges will apply.
There is no additional charge for data transferred in and out of the Amazon RDS database instance.

note: The pricing page gives a per-GB EC2 rate without a Region, so the amount is not recorded.

claim: A DB snapshot copy to another Region is charged for the data transferred, and the copy is then charged as snapshot storage in the destination Region.
question: What do you pay for copying an RDS snapshot to another Region?

evidence.quote: DB snapshot copy is charged for the data transferred to copy the snapshot data across Regions.
When the snapshot is copied, standard Amazon RDS database snapshot charges will apply to store it in the destination Region.

claim: Cross-Region automated backups are charged for the data transferred to copy the snapshot and transaction logs across Regions, plus snapshot storage in the destination Region; storing the transaction logs has no additional charge.
question: What do cross-Region automated backups cost for Amazon RDS?

values.display: no additional charge for storage of the DB transaction logs

evidence.quote: Cross-Region automated backups are charged for the data transferred to copy the Amazon RDS DB snapshot and DB transaction logs across Regions.
There is no additional charge for storage of the DB transaction logs.

claim: The RDS pricing page says Reserved Instances can save up to 69% over on-demand rates for steady-state use, with a one- or three-year term.
question: How much can RDS Reserved Instances save compared with On-Demand?

evidence.quote: You can save up to 69% when you use Reserved Instances over on-demand rates when used in steady state
With Reserved Instances, you can reserve a DB instance for a one- or three-year term.

claim: With On-Demand Instances you pay for compute capacity per hour the DB instance runs, with no long-term commitment; AWS recommends them for short-term, spiky or unpredictable workloads that cannot be interrupted.
question: When does AWS recommend RDS On-Demand Instances?

evidence.quote: With On-Demand Instances, you pay for compute capacity per hour your DB instance runs.
Applications with short-term, spiky, or unpredictable workloads that cannot be interrupted

claim: Multi-AZ deployments cost more than Single-AZ deployments and can cost approximately twice as much, because of the additional standby instance and its resources.
question: How does the cost of an RDS Multi-AZ deployment compare with Single-AZ?

evidence.quote: Due to the additional resources and increased availability, Multi-AZ deployments are priced higher than Single-AZ deployments, and can cost approximately twice as much due to the additional standby instance and associated resources.

claim: Read replicas are billed as standard DB instances at the rate of their DB instance class, and replication data transfer between a source and a read replica in the same Region is free.
question: How are RDS read replicas billed?

evidence.quote: Read replicas are billed as standard DB instances at the same rates as the DB instance class used for the replica.
You aren't charged for the data transfer incurred in replicating data between the source DB instance and a read replica within the same AWS Region.

claim: An RDS resource in a VPC with a public IPv4 address incurs the standard public IPv4 address charges.
question: Does a publicly accessible RDS DB instance pay for its public IPv4 address?

evidence.quote: You will incur standard public IPv4 address charges associated with a resource launched in an Amazon VPC.

claim: RDS Extended Support is a paid offering that gives you more time to upgrade to a supported major engine version.
question: Is RDS Extended Support free?

values.display: This paid offering gives you more time

evidence.quote: This paid offering gives you more time to upgrade to a supported major engine version.

claim: For provisioned instances on Aurora, RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQL Server, RDS Proxy is priced per vCPU per hour of the underlying database instances.
question: How is Amazon RDS Proxy priced for provisioned DB instances?

evidence.quote: RDS Proxy is priced based on the capacity of underlying instances.
For provisioned instances on Amazon Aurora, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, Amazon RDS for MySQL, Amazon RDS for MariaDB, and Amazon RDS for SQL Server, RDS Proxy is priced per vCPU per hour.

claim: The default endpoint of an RDS Proxy has no additional charge; each extra proxy endpoint provisions an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint, which has its own charges.
question: Do RDS Proxy endpoints cost extra?

values.display: no additional charges associated with the default endpoint

evidence.quote: There are no additional charges associated with the default endpoint you get when you create an RDS Proxy.
Adding a RDS Proxy endpoint provisions an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint, which incurs additional charges as described on the PrivateLink pricing page.
